title: Two Pointers & Sliding Window
summary: Use indexes that move with a rule instead of trying every possible pair or slice.
refresher: Two pointers track two positions. A sliding window tracks a start and end around a current range. Move the pointer that helps the rule become true or stay true.
refresher_code:
left = 0
for right in range(n): update window

sections.title: Two pointers
sections.summary: Two indexes let you compare two positions without nested loops.

blocks.body: Two pointers are useful when the data is sorted or when you need to compare both ends. One pointer might move from the left while the other moves from the right.

blocks.caption: The pointer move should follow the reason from the problem.
blocks.right: Move left when the sum is too small; move right when it is too large

blocks.prompt: What makes two pointers better than checking every pair?
choices: Each move removes choices you no longer need
It removes the need for conditions
blocks.why: The pointer rule narrows the search instead of trying every combination.

sections.title: Sliding window
sections.summary: A window is a current slice of the data.

blocks.body: A sliding window grows by moving the right edge. When the window breaks a rule, shrink it by moving the left edge.

blocks.caption: The window grows to include each new value, then shrinks while it is too large.

python.code:
left = 0
current = 0
for right, value in enumerate(nums):
    current += value
    while current > limit:
        current -= nums[left]
        left += 1

blocks.prompt: When should the left side of a sliding window move?
choices: When the current window breaks the rule
Only at the end of the program
blocks.why: The left pointer shrinks the window until the rule is true again.
